sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: CrewAI is an open-source Python framework for building teams of AI agents. You give each agent a role, a goal and tools, assign them tasks, and they work together to finish multi-step jobs like research and report writing.
sixtySeconds.problem: A single prompt or chatbot struggles with multi-step work that needs research, tools and review. CrewAI splits that work across specialised agents (Crews) and lets you wrap them in event-driven workflows with explicit control (Flows).
whoFor: Builders who want agents plus plain Python business logic
Learners following the DeepLearning.AI CrewAI courses
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it when you want role-based agents that collaborate, plus precise workflow control in regular Python, in one framework that runs from prototype to production.
requirements: An API key for your model provider (OpenAI by default)

overview: CrewAI has two building blocks. Crews are teams of autonomous agents with roles, goals and backstories that delegate and collaborate. Flows are event-driven workflows with state, branching and routing that can call single LLMs or whole Crews.

The crewai CLI scaffolds a project: agents live in agents/*.jsonc, tasks and crew settings in crew.jsonc, and crewai run loads them. A --classic option creates the older Python/YAML layout. Agents use the OpenAI API by default, and the docs show how to connect other providers, including local models through Ollama.
CrewAI is MIT licensed. It sends anonymous telemetry by default, which you can turn off with OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true. A commercial AMP Suite adds managed deployment and observability.

steps.title: Edit the agents
steps.body: Set each agent's role, goal, backstory, model and tools in agents/*.jsonc. Use {topic} placeholders and set a default under inputs in crew.jsonc.

steps.body: Put your model provider key, and SERPER_API_KEY if you use web search, in the .env file.
